title: Relocate App-Located Generic Engine Crates Into Framework Surface
description: F4: Relocate the app-located but mechanism-generic engine crates into the framework, and replace the hardcoded per-app engine-loader code in framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx with a single generic loader table keyed by surface kind (paint-2d, tiled-map, board-2d, node-graph, terrain). Target crates: gis/2d/rs's MapHost/MapSession engine -> framework/surface/tiled-map/rs (keep gis's own domain document model in gis/plugin/rs); puzzle/2d/rs's BoardHost/board-hosting engine -> framework/surface/board/rs; raster/rs's session host -> framework/surface/paint/rs (raster's document schema/ops stay in raster/plugin/rs); gis/3d/rs's terrain sampler -> framework/surface/terrain/rs; flow/core's node-graph engine -> a framework surface home for node-graph. Bring the script.ts+project.json+package.json triad with each crate. Update workspace Cargo.toml members, root package.json workspaces, framework/renderer/wgpu Cargo.toml deps, and any other Cargo.toml path deps referencing the old crate paths. Parent should be 26/07/17/GENERALIZE-APPS-ONTO-FRAMEWORK-PRIMITIVES but that id is not recognized by ticket_open; opening top-level, noting in close summary.
summary:
Relocated 4 of the 5 named app-located engine crates into framework/surface/*, splitting engine-mechanism code from each app's own domain/document model, and consolidated os-shell.tsx's 5 hardcoded per-app WASM dynamic-import blocks into one generic table-driven loader.

MOVES (old -> new):
- gis/2d/rs -> framework/surface/tiled-map/rs (crate `gis_2d` -> `framework_surface_tiled_map`, pkg `@semio-tech/gis-2d-rs` -> `@semio-tech/framework-surface-tiled-map-rs`). Split: MapHost/MapSession/tiles/projection/vector_tiles engine (4000 lines) moved; the self-contained DocumentVcs+Feature+OpenUrl domain block (~340 lines: GisMapDocument/GisMapDiff/GisMapOp/MapFeature/MapFeaturePatch/GisMapDocumentVcs/open_url) moved into gis/plugin/rs as a new `pub(crate) mod domain`.
- gis/3d/rs -> framework/surface/terrain/rs (crate `gis_3d` -> `framework_surface_terrain`, pkg -> `@semio-tech/framework-surface-terrain-rs`). Split: same pattern; the DocumentVcs block (Gis3dTerrainDocument/Diff/Op, ~60 lines) moved into gis/plugin/rs's new domain module; one test that exercised it moved conceptually with it (removed from the engine crate's test mod, since gis/plugin/rs already exercises the same ops via its own app_3d tests).
- raster/rs -> framework/surface/paint/rs (crate `raster` -> `framework_surface_paint`, pkg -> `@semio-tech/framework-surface-paint-rs`). Split: RasterHost/RasterSession engine (1390 lines) moved; the self-contained DocumentVcs block (RasterProjection/RasterLayerNode/RasterOp/RasterDiff/RasterDocumentVcs, ~650 lines) moved into raster/plugin/rs as a new `pub(crate) mod domain`.
- framework/graph/rs -> framework/surface/node-graph/rs (crate `framework_graph` -> `framework_surface_node_graph`, pkg -> `@semio-tech/framework-surface-node-graph-rs`). Whole-crate relocation, no split needed (already 100% generic: GraphHost + GraphSession, zero domain leakage).

JUDGMENT CALL — flow/core and puzzle/2d/rs's BoardHost NOT relocated: investigated both against the ticket's premise ("already generic in mechanism but app-located") and found it doesn't hold for either. (1) flow/core/rs (6181 lines) is NOT a generic node-graph engine — it's flow-app's own execution engine tightly coupled to flow_module_brep/bim/draw/dictionary/list/logic/math/text, neural_engine/neural_dag, kernel_3d_engine, mathematical_graph_manifest; the actually-generic node-graph rendering/session engine (GraphHost+GraphSession) was already correctly framework-owned at framework/graph/rs, which is what I relocated instead. (2) puzzle/2d/rs's `BoardHost` struct is not defined in puzzle/2d/rs at all — it already lives in `infinite/board/port/directed/normal/rs` (a generic graph-topology crate) and is merely re-exported into puzzle/2d/rs via `pub use infinite_board_port_directed_normal::{self as graph, *}`. What remains in puzzle/2d/rs (BoardSession WASM binding, icon codec, Puzzle2dExtension, Puzzle2dOp/Diff) is more tightly coupled (icon-lookup injection, fixture/document glue) and splitting it safely needs its own careful pass; additionally an unrelated, still-open concurrent ticket (26/07/18/GENERALIZE-PUZZLE2D-BOARD-SURFACE-TO-BOARD2D) is actively mid-edit on puzzle_2d/framework-renderer-wgpu/ui-wgpu in this exact area, raising collision risk. Left puzzle/2d/rs and flow/core/rs untouched; the os-shell.tsx loader table still includes a `board-2d` entry, it simply still points at the unchanged `@semio-tech/puzzle-2d-rs` package. Flagging both for a follow-up wave.

OS-SHELL.TSX CONSOLIDATION: replaced the 5 near-identical `let xPromise; export async function createX() { if (!xPromise) { xPromise = import("pkg").then(...) } ... return new mod.X() }` blocks (GraphSession/RasterSession/MapSession/TerrainSession/Board2dSession) with one `//#region 🔖️EngineSessionLoader` (a `Record<string, () => Promise<Module>>` import table keyed by surface kind — node-graph/paint-2d/tiled-map/terrain/board-2d — plus one cached-promise-per-kind generic `createEngineSession<TSession>(kind, className)` helper). Each `createXSession` export is now a 1-line call into that helper; exported function names and public TS types (RasterWasmSession, MapWasmSession, TerrainWasmSession, Board2dWasmSession, GraphWasmSession) are unchanged so no host component call sites needed touching. FlowSession and EditorSession were deliberately left as their own separate hand-rolled blocks (out of scope — not part of the 4 relocated engines; FlowSession's TS shape is a large flow-specific superset of GraphWasmSession chosen at runtime by scene content, not by surface kind). Also fixed a pre-existing region-tag bug in this area (MapSession's region never closed; Board2dWasmSession's content closed under a wrong `//#endregion MapSession` tag) — now MapSession/TerrainSession/Board2dSession each have correct open/close region tags.

OTHER FILES UPDATED (path/name repoints only, no logic change): Cargo.toml (workspace members), package.json (root workspaces + framework/renderer/react deps), framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/Cargo.toml + lib.rs (gis_2d::MapHost -> framework_surface_tiled_map::MapHost at 8 call sites; framework_graph::GraphHost -> framework_surface_node_graph::GraphHost), gis/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml+lib.rs (new domain module, split imports, added wasm32 wasm-bindgen/web-sys deps that used to arrive transitively via the old gis_2d dependency), raster/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml+lib.rs (same pattern), puzzle/2d/rs/Cargo.toml+lib.rs (dropped the dead, zero-consumer `gis_2d` dep and its `pub use gis_2d as map;` re-export), framework/product/os/dev/script.ts (dev-server wasm prebuild script paths for gis2d/gis3d, + added a missing `raster` case following the same pattern), framework/product/os/dev/js/vite.config.ts (optimizeDeps exclude list), ui/styling/vite-elements-assets.ts (dev wasm-stub resolver's special-cased framework-graph-rs path), ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs (one doc-comment path reference).

VERIFICATION:
- `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` on all 6 touched/created Rust files (framework/surface/{terrain,tiled-map,paint}/rs/lib.rs, gis/plugin/rs/lib.rs, raster/plugin/rs/lib.rs, puzzle/2d/rs/lib.rs) — PASSED (parses as valid Rust; only formatting-style diffs, no syntax errors).
- `cargo metadata --no-deps` — PASSED (full valid dependency graph resolved, confirming every Cargo.toml path dependency I touched/added points at a real, correctly-shaped manifest).
- `cargo check -p framework_surface_terrain -p framework_surface_tiled_map -p framework_surface_paint -p framework_surface_node_graph` — STARTED, DID NOT COMPLETE. Blocked ~7+ minutes at 0% CPU on the shared workspace build-directory lock under extreme concurrent contention (158 concurrent cargo/rustc processes system-wide from other active sessions at time of check, matching the repo's known "Concurrent Cargo Workspace Churn" pattern). Left running in background; genuinely unconfirmed at type-check/borrow-check level — flagging for a follow-up check once the shared build queue clears.
- `bun install` — FAILED, but due to a pre-existing, unrelated breakage: `package.json` workspace entry `"mathematical/graph/port/directed/dag"` points at a directory that does not exist on disk. Confirmed via `git diff package.json` that this line is NOT part of my change (my diff to package.json is a clean 4-line add/4-line remove in the gis/raster/graph section only) — this is another concurrent session's in-progress rename, out of my ticket's scope. Left untouched per the "don't chase concurrent churn" guidance.
- `bunx vitest run framework/renderer/react` — ran despite the blocked install (node_modules pre-existed): failed on `index.test.ts` with "Failed to resolve import '@semio-tech/framework-surface-node-graph-rs/pkg/framework_surface_node_graph.js'" — expected/benign, since `bun install` (blocked above) hasn't yet registered the renamed workspace package in node_modules. Confirms the TS edit is syntactically valid and correctly emits the new import specifiers; full resolution needs `bun install` to succeed first (blocked by the unrelated issue above).
- Full repo grep sweep for all five old crate names (as Rust `::` paths, Cargo `path =` deps, and `@semio-tech/*` npm specifiers) — zero remaining hits outside `.repo/` ticket backups and other sessions' worktrees.

NOT VERIFIED / FOLLOW-UP NEEDED: `cargo check --workspace` (or at least the four relocated crates + their dependents: gis-plugin, raster-plugin, semio-framework-renderer-wgpu, semio-framework-core) once the shared build lock clears; `bun install` + `bun vitest run framework/renderer/react` once the unrelated `mathematical/graph/port/directed/dag` workspace entry is fixed by whichever session owns that; a real split of puzzle/2d/rs's board-hosting session code and a re-examination of whether flow/core needs any generalization, both flagged above as out of scope for this pass.
